importantNotes: Esther is one of only two books that never mention God by name (Song of Solomon is the other).
'For such a time as this' (4:14) — God places people where they can make a difference.
The Feast of Purim (still celebrated today) was established to remember this deliverance.
The story demonstrates that God works behind the scenes even when He seems silent.
The reversal theme: Haman builds a gallows for Mordecai but is hanged on it himself.

chapters.1: Queen Vashti refuses King Xerxes' command and is deposed.
chapters.2: Esther becomes queen; Mordecai uncovers a plot to assassinate the king.
chapters.3: Haman is promoted; he plots to destroy all Jews because Mordecai refuses to bow to him.
chapters.4: Mordecai urges Esther to intervene — 'for such a time as this.'
chapters.5: Esther invites the king and Haman to a banquet; Haman builds a gallows for Mordecai.
chapters.6: The king honors Mordecai after reading about his loyalty; Haman must lead the honor.
chapters.7: Esther reveals Haman's plot; the king orders Haman hanged on his own gallows.
chapters.8: Mordecai receives Haman's position; a new decree allows the Jews to defend themselves.
chapters.9: The Jews defeat their enemies; the Feast of Purim is established.
chapters.10: Mordecai is second in rank to King Xerxes and works for the good of his people.
